original.target_description: Study 1: question-level quadratic relationship between mean trajectory sample entropy and distance from equibiased truth probability (.5), comparing middle- with low- and high-truth-value questions; Figure 1d.

n.location: Published p. 22 (PDF p. 1), Method; p. 23 (PDF p. 2), Figure 1d and caption; target test on p. 24 (PDF p. 3).
n.quote: The data for this study come from 141 college-age participants … (97 females, 44 males) who responded to 11 yes/no questions … presented in random order over headphones.
n.sample_role: Question-level observations: mean trajectory sample entropy for each of 11 yes/no questions. Source participant sample: 141 college-age participants; participant total is not the n of this question-level test.
n.exclusions: No question or participant exclusions reported for this test. The 54 participants with reversed response positions were retained and mirror-reversed.

es.location: Published p. 24 (PDF p. 3), Results and Discussion, left column, sample-entropy paragraph referring to Figure 1d.
es.quote: Sample entropy was higher for middle-truth-value questions … than for low- and high-truth-value questions (see Fig. 1d), … quadratic r 5 .70, F(1, 9) 5 8.7, p < .05, prep 5 .939.

p.location: Published p. 24 (PDF p. 3), Results and Discussion, left column, sample-entropy paragraph referring to Figure 1d.

notes: Original-only blind validation. Published 2008 Short Report, pp. 22–24. Title/authors verified on rendered PDF p. 1; all three article pages visually inspected. Source PDF: /home/lukas/work/fred-mac-recovery-20261030/continuation-1201/private_batch_02/artifacts/6a339cfac4ba90441dc57a35_ebsco.pdf. Quotations retain canonical-text glyphs/line breaks, with explicit ellipsis for omitted text. Canonical math-font extraction renders equals signs as 5 and omits the minus before .70; rendered p. 24 clearly prints quadratic r = −.70, F(1, 9) = 8.7, p < .05. The numeric effect value preserves the visually verified negative sign. Figure 1d and caption establish question means as the observations; Method explicitly prints 11 questions, corresponding to the 11 plotted observations. No metric conversion or statistic calculation performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
